clue.text: Rabbit with mate about cold

indicators.note: the slang word for a friend goes around the word for coldness, enclosing it

blocks.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, shortened to china
a chill is a cold

explanation.surface: A pet rabbit huddles beside its companion to keep off the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang keeps only the first word of the rhyme: china plate means mate, so mate is china.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinchilla is a breed of domestic rabbit with soft grey fur, named after the South American rodent.

clue.text: Bubbly winner, a girl, stopping short

indicators.note: stopping short of the end, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: short for champion
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl celebrating a win with bubbly stops before the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAMP + AGNE(s). Bubbly is everyday slang for sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubbly is the informal name for sparkling wine, especially the famous French one from Reims and Épernay.

clue.text: Load up during delay

blocks.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
to stall is to delay

explanation.surface: Cargo is loaded while waiting through a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To install software is to load it onto a computer and set it up ready for use.

clue.text: Dashing Earl's first to change more than one title

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, the only one kept
the letters are changed, rearranged into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of Earl

explanation.surface: A dashing earl is the first to change his several titles.
explanation.walkthrough: Titles here are headings on a page, not aristocratic ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Headings are the titles printed above chapters or sections, and the plural covers several.

clue.text: At heart, learner bad in matching solving approach?

indicators.note: a bad arrangement is a corrupted one, so the letters before it are jumbled
the jumbled group is placed inside the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written, not as a centre-letter signal
L for learner, from the L-plate
linking things is matching them up

explanation.surface: A poor learner tries to match things up by heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At heart' wants to pick the middle of learner, but it is fodder: AT HEART + L, jumbled, goes inside LINKING after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral thinking means tackling problems by indirect, creative routes, a method for puzzles; the question mark flags it as one example.

clue.text: A double-headed flower getting trimmed to gain recognition

indicators.note: trimming cuts off the tail, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written
a second head: the flower's first letter is doubled
crossword flower: something that flows

explanation.surface: A freak two-headed bloom is pruned so it wins a prize at the show.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower is the crossword river, a thing that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive is to become successful and established, achieving fame or recognition in one's field.

clue.text: Cut source of energy getting hot

blocks.note: gas is a fuel
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A power cut means the energy supply is getting hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash is a long deep wound or slash, so the noun cut fits it as a synonym.

clue.text: Verging on collapse being in charge

indicators.note: something that collapses falls apart, so the letters are scattered and reset

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A regime close to falling apart is still in power.
explanation.definitionFit: Governing means ruling or controlling, so a governing body is the one with authority.

clue.text: Queer Street continued, for example, spinning

indicators.note: spinning round turns the short abbreviation back to front

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
ran on, kept going
eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia

explanation.surface: Queer Street goes on and on, a spinning example.
explanation.walkthrough: Queer Street is an old British phrase for financial difficulty, but here Queer is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Queer in its older sense means odd or peculiar, which is what strange means.

clue.text: Remove a bishop's small pamphlet

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, with the possessive S
a tract is a short religious or political pamphlet

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take away a bishop's little leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: A + B'S + TRACT. The verb abstract means to take out or extract.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract something is to withdraw or take it away, as in abstracting funds from an account.

clue.text: Echo returning note ... right

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the whole string is read from the end

blocks.note: a breve is a long note in music
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An echo sends a note back, and rightly so.
explanation.walkthrough: BREVE then R, the whole run backwards, gives REVERB.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverb is reverberation, sound bouncing back off surfaces, which is an echo effect in recording.

clue.text: Some got energy from this power breakfast

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
used as a verb: to breakfast is to eat

explanation.surface: A hearty breakfast gives people energy for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power breakfast' reads as one meal; split it, and breakfast is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Peat is dug and burned as fuel, so people have long got heat and energy from it.

clue.text: Cheeky retriever bounding around the end of garden

indicators.note: a dog bounding around is leaping about all over, so the letters are thrown into disorder
the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of garden

explanation.surface: A cheeky dog dashes round the bottom of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Irreverent means lacking proper respect, which is what a cheeky person shows.

clue.text: Plant is a heather whipped by windy weather

indicators.note: something whipped by the wind is caught up within it, so these letters sit inside

blocks.note: taken as written
ling is common heather
a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A heather plant is battered by stormy weather on the moor.
explanation.walkthrough: Ling is the usual name for common heather on British moors.
explanation.definitionFit: Galingale is a sedge, and also a ginger-family plant whose aromatic root is used as a spice.

clue.text: Step in and lay to rest Venerable Bede at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the name before it

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
Ven. is the abbreviation for Venerable, an ecclesiastical title
the final letter of Bede

explanation.surface: Someone steps in to bury the Venerable Bede at last.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venerable Bede was an Anglo-Saxon monk and historian.
explanation.definitionFit: To intervene is to come between parties or interfere in a situation, stepping into it.

clue.text: Cyclist's condition

blocks.note: first meaning: one who rides a bicycle
second meaning: a clause added to a document or agreement

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a cyclist's state of health; the 's is 'is', joining two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone on a bike is a rider, and a rider is also an extra stipulation attached to a contract or verdict.

clue.text: Memo about a book going cheap

indicators.note: lying about something surrounds it, so the memo word goes round the letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a memo is a note to jog the memory

explanation.surface: A publisher's memo concerns a book being sold off cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: REM(A)INDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A remainder is an unsold copy of a book that the publisher offloads at a reduced price.

clue.text: Flower holder, being cheap, broken in bed

indicators.note: something broken falls into pieces, so its letters are rearranged
placed in the bed, so these letters sit inside the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A cheap vase for flowers got broken in a flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bed looks like a flower bed; it is a cot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cachepot is an ornamental container for hiding a plain plant pot, so it holds flowers.

clue.text: Cream caramel — it excites to some extent

indicators.note: only partly present, so the word lies within part of the phrase before it

blocks.note: letters running across the words

explanation.surface: A crème caramel is thrillingly good, up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden in caramEL IT Excites. Cream looks like part of the pudding, but stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, just as the elite is the best group.

clue.text: Fat end of foot caught up in that outfit

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so backwards
caught in means held inside, so the turned part goes within

blocks.note: lard is pig fat
the toe is at the end of the foot

explanation.surface: A fat dancer's toe gets caught up in the outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the turned piece reads upwards; 'that' only points at the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is a close-fitting one-piece garment worn by dancers and gymnasts, a kind of outfit.

clue.text: Foodstuff with piquancy, precious item containing curry at its heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, the only one kept
holding something inside, so the next letter goes within the jewel

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
piquant food has heat
a gem is a precious stone
the central letter of curry

explanation.surface: A spicy dish with a jewel of a curry in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: W + HEAT + GE(R)M.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheatgerm is the nutritious embryo of the wheat grain, sold and eaten as a health food.

clue.text: At first, eat endlessly durable protein

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word after it
with no end, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: the opening letter of eat
durable things are lasting

explanation.surface: Diet advice: eat protein first, and keep eating it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastin is the stretchy structural protein in skin and connective tissue that lets them spring back.

clue.text: Vent feelings in day out in Dieppe?

blocks.note: a French town calls for the French article le
a day trip

explanation.surface: A traveller lets off steam on an excursion to Dieppe.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a French-style phrase: 'le trip', the day out as it might be said in Dieppe, a French Channel port.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is to speak or act without restraint, releasing pent-up emotion freely.

clue.text: Juvenile visiting a quarter for St Valentine's Day?

indicators.note: a visitor stays inside another's place, so these letters go within

blocks.note: a teen is a young person
a quarter is one fourth

explanation.surface: A teenager calls on a neighbourhood on Valentine's Day.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition only names a date: St Valentine's Day is 14 February.
explanation.definitionFit: St Valentine's Day falls on the fourteenth of February, so the ordinal names that date.

clue.text: Not entirely wonderful present suppliers

indicators.note: not the entire word, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: magic as an adjective means wonderful

explanation.surface: Some gifts are not quite wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: MAGIC loses its last letter. Present here is a noun, a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: The three wise men brought gold, frankincense and myrrh as gifts to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Eg, sleeper always in occupation

blocks.note: a sleeper is a railway car with beds
e'er, the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Someone is always asleep at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Sleeper looks like a person dozing; it is the railway carriage with berths.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is one's profession or lifelong line of work, which an occupation also names.

clue.text: Island holiday destination stocked with booze from abroad

indicators.note: a place stocked with goods has them inside it, so these letters go within

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for island
the Med, the Mediterranean, a favourite British holiday spot
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: An island resort has laid in plenty of drink from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: I + ME(PORT)D.
explanation.definitionFit: Imported goods are brought in from another country, so they come from abroad.

clue.text: One had an article in French — that's pointless

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the contraction 'd, as in I'd for I had
le is the French masculine article

explanation.surface: A student grumbles that studying a French article was a waste of time.
explanation.walkthrough: One had = I'D, plus LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk or threats are futile and without purpose, which is what pointless means.

clue.text: There's no getting away from this p-painter

definitions.text: There's no getting away from this

blocks.note: p is the standard abbreviation for page
J. M. W. Turner, the English landscape painter

explanation.surface: Someone stammers over a painter they cannot escape.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered 'p-' is not a stutter but the abbreviation for page.
explanation.definitionFit: A page-turner is a gripping book that readers cannot put down, so there is no escaping it.
